answer: Histories are stored in plume, checked in summit, and umber shows each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 8 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 2192 identities would post 582 proofs and burn roughly 47 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
